meta.title: Operation of Soxhlet Extraction Apparatus in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To perform continuous hot solvent extraction of phytochemicals from crude drugs using the Soxhlet method for determination of extractive values and isolation of specific compound classes as per IP/WHO requirements.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for determination of alcohol-soluble, water-soluble, and ether-soluble extractive values of crude drugs, and for preparative isolation of specific phytochemical classes.
procedure: Weigh the dried, powdered crude drug accurately (typically 2–5 g for extractive value; 20–50 g for preparative extraction) and record the weight.

Prepare the thimble: place a small plug of cotton wool at the bottom of the extraction thimble, then pack the drug powder uniformly; place another cotton plug on top — the drug should not be packed so tightly as to prevent solvent flow.
Ensure the thimble height does not exceed the siphon arm level of the Soxhlet extractor.
Assemble the apparatus from bottom to top: round-bottom flask → Soxhlet extractor body → Liebig condenser.
Add the extraction solvent to the round-bottom flask: typically 1.5–2× the extractor volume (e.g., 150–200 mL for a 100 mL Soxhlet); add boiling chips.
Insert the filled thimble into the Soxhlet extractor body.
Connect coolant water to the condenser (inlet at bottom, outlet at top) and confirm steady flow.
Heat the flask using a heating mantle or water bath — bring solvent to a gentle boil.
As the solvent evaporates, condenses, and fills the Soxhlet chamber, it contacts the drug in the thimble, extracting soluble compounds.
When the Soxhlet chamber fills to the siphon level, the solution automatically siphons back into the flask — this completes one cycle.
Maintain extraction for the required number of cycles or time per the IP method (typically 16–25 cycles or 4–8 hours for extractive values).
Monitor the solvent level in the flask periodically — add more solvent if it falls below 1/3 flask volume.
After extraction, reduce heat and allow the extractor to cool; allow one final siphon cycle.
Remove the thimble with forceps (it is hot); allow to cool.
Transfer the flask extract to a pre-weighed evaporating dish.
Evaporate the solvent on a water bath at appropriate temperature; dry in an oven at 105°C to constant weight.
Calculate extractive value (%): [(Weight of extract) / (Weight of drug)] × 100.
Record extraction solvent, number of cycles, time, initial drug weight, and extractive value in the logbook.
precautions: Never use flammable solvents (ether, petroleum ether) without a spark-free heating source — use a water bath, not a heating mantle, for highly flammable solvents.
Work in a fume hood for all volatile organic solvents.
Do not pack the thimble too tight — restricted flow prevents proper extraction cycles.
Ensure the drug level in the thimble is below the siphon arm — drug above the siphon arm does not get extracted.
Use boiling chips to prevent bumping — bumping causes spillage of hot solvent.
Never leave the Soxhlet extraction unattended for prolonged periods — coolant supply failure causes uncondensed vapours to escape.
Ensure all joints are tight — leaking joints allow solvent vapour escape and fire risk.
Cool the apparatus before disassembling — hot ground glass joints may seize.
